newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends flat amid tight liqudity.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends flat amid tight liqudity.

text.p: High money market rates kept the Sri Lankan rupee in a tight range against the dollar throughout Wednesday before closing little changed from Tuesday, dealers said.
The rupee ended at 56.18 against 56.12 on Tuesday.
"The first trade for the day took place only two hours after the market opened at around 56.18," said a Sampath Bank dealer, adding the trading range remined in a few local cents throughout the day.
The overnight call rate, which at one point reached 19 percent, ended at 16.5 against 16 yesterday, dealers said.
Dealers said the rupee would have gone lower unless the rupee liquidity was tight on the money market.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by three cents, setting buying and selling rates at 55.6974 and 56.8226.
The Central Bank said it bought treasury bills totalling 1.2 billion rupees at today's auctions, which dealers say should ease money rates.
